ai.description: Jerdon’s sea snake reaches 100 cm. It is yellowish-olive with 30–50 dark crossbars. Key features include a small head, keeled ventral scales, and a distinctively spiny appearance due to rhomboid scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis jerdonii* is uniquely identified by its strongly keeled, overlapping scales that form distinct longitudinal ridges along the body, unlike the smooth scales of most other sea snakes.
ai.habitat: Jerdon's sea snake inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries of the Indian subcontinent, often frequenting areas with muddy or sandy substrates and mangrove fringes.
ai.behavior: Jerdon's sea snakes are primarily nocturnal hunters that forage for small fish and crustaceans along the seafloor in shallow coastal waters.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis jerdonii* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to 3–16 live young. Breeding occurs between March and May in Indian waters.
ai.distributionRemarks: Jerdon's sea snake inhabits coastal waters along the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Bay of Bengal to the Arabian Sea, typically at shallow depths.
